tex_content.html:
Proposition
1. ch6:6.37

Let $U$ be a normal neighborhood of $P$. There are unique objects consisting of a continuous function $r:U\to [0,\infty )$ and a smooth vector field $\partial _r$ on $U\setminus P$ such that in every Fermi coordinate system $(x^1,\ldots ,x^k,v^1,\ldots ,v^{n-k})$, \begin{equation} r(x,v)=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+\cdots +(v^{n-k})^2}, \tag {6.17} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \partial _r =\frac{v^1}{r(x,v)}\frac{\partial }{\partial v^1} +\cdots + \frac{v^{n-k}}{r(x,v)}\frac{\partial }{\partial v^{n-k}}. \tag {6.18} \end{equation} Moreover, $r$ is smooth on $U\setminus P$, and $r^2$ is smooth on $U$.

Proof

\sketch Let $V\subseteq NP$ be mapped diffeomorphically onto $U$ by the normal exponential map $E$, put $\rho (p,v)=|v|_g$, and define $r=\rho \circ E^{-1}$. An orthonormal local frame of $NP$ gives (6.17), which also proves the asserted regularity.

For $q=\exp _p(v)\in U\setminus P$, let $\gamma (t)=\exp _p(tv)$ and define

\begin{equation} \partial _r|_q=\frac1{r(q)}\gamma '(1). \tag {6.19} \end{equation}

In Fermi coordinates, $\gamma (t)=(x^1,\ldots ,x^k,tv^1,\ldots ,tv^{n-k})$, so (6.19) gives (6.18), independently of the chosen coordinates.

□

The objects $r$ and $\partial _r$ are respectively the radial distance function and radial vector field for $P$.
